title: What To Prepare Before A Legal Consultation
description: A practical checklist for organizing facts, documents, deadlines, and questions before speaking with a lawyer.
hero: A useful consultation starts before the meeting. The clearer your facts and documents are, the easier it is to identify risk and choose the next step.

sections.title: Start with the timeline
sections.body: Write the important dates in order, including agreements, payments, notices, meetings, filings, and deadlines. A timeline helps counsel separate urgent facts from background detail.

sections.title: Bring the primary documents
sections.body: Share signed agreements, deeds, notices, company papers, citizenship copies, letters, receipts, messages, and any court or government documents connected to the matter.

sections.title: Name the parties clearly
sections.body: List the people, companies, offices, and representatives involved. Include phone numbers, addresses, relationship context, and the role each person played.

title: Do Not Ignore A Legal Notice
description: Why legal notices should be reviewed quickly, even when the facts feel simple or the demand seems unfair.
hero: A legal notice is not just a letter. It can set dates, preserve claims, shape negotiation, and create avoidable risk when left unanswered.

sections.title: Check the deadline first
sections.body: Some notices expect a reply within a stated period. Even when the deadline is not final, delay can weaken negotiation position or make the other side's version look uncontested.

sections.title: Review the facts before replying
sections.body: A fast emotional response can create problems. Compare the notice against documents, messages, payment records, ownership papers, and previous communication before deciding what to say.

sections.title: Choose the response path
sections.body: The right next step may be a formal reply, a request for documents, settlement communication, preservation of evidence, or preparation for filing.

title: Contract Review Before Signing
description: A short guide to reviewing obligations, payment terms, exit rights, and dispute clauses before signing a contract.
hero: The best time to understand a contract is before the signature, when risk can still be priced, revised, or rejected.

sections.title: Read obligations both ways
sections.body: A contract should make each party's responsibilities clear. Review what must be delivered, when it must happen, what proof is required, and what happens when performance is late.

sections.title: Check payment and termination
sections.body: Payment dates, penalties, refunds, termination rights, renewal terms, and notice periods often matter more in a dispute than the general promises at the top of the agreement.

sections.title: Understand the dispute clause
sections.body: Jurisdiction, arbitration, governing law, notice method, and document language can change how expensive and practical enforcement becomes.
